## Represent objects and transformations numerically

::: {.concept-grid}
<div><span class="diagram-label">scalar $a$</span><br>one quantity<br><span class="small">temperature</span></div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">vector $\vct{x}$</span><br>several related quantities<br><span class="small">coordinates or pixel values</span></div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">matrix $\mat{A}$</span><br>a transformation or relationships<br><span class="small">geometric action or constraints</span></div>
:::

::: {.key-point}
Coordinates and arrays let us compute with these objects, but the representation is not the object itself.
:::

::: {.diagram-flow}
<div class="diagram-node">input object or state<br>$\vct{x}$</div>
<div class="diagram-arrow">$\longmapsto$</div>
<div class="diagram-node">action or relationships<br>$\mat{A}$</div>
<div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">resulting object or state<br>$\vct{y}=\mat{A}\vct{x}$</div>
:::

::: {.concept-grid}
<div>transform an image or geometric object</div>
<div>mix related quantities</div>
<div>update a network state or express constraints</div>
:::

## An arrow is only the beginning

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 300" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Vector arrow from the origin to the point 3 comma 2"><defs><marker id="vector-arrowhead" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0,10 3.5,0 7" fill="#007acc"/></marker></defs><path d="M55 245H380M55 245V30" stroke="#555" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M55 245L315 80" stroke="#007acc" stroke-width="8" marker-end="url(#vector-arrowhead)"/><text x="322" y="74" font-size="28">(3, 2)</text></svg>
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
A vector can record

- a direction and displacement
- several measurements at once
- the current state of a system
- the ingredients of an object

$$
\vct{x}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\2\end{bmatrix}
$$
:::
:::

## A tiny image becomes numbers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}

<div class="pixel-grid" aria-label="Four by four grayscale pixel image">
<span data-shade="17"></span><span data-shade="51"></span><span data-shade="221"></span><span data-shade="238"></span>
<span data-shade="34"></span><span data-shade="119"></span><span data-shade="238"></span><span data-shade="187"></span>
<span data-shade="204"></span><span data-shade="238"></span><span data-shade="102"></span><span data-shade="34"></span>
<span data-shade="238"></span><span data-shade="170"></span><span data-shade="34"></span><span data-shade="17"></span>
</div>

:::

::: {.column width="58%"}
Choose an order; read off brightness

$$
\vct{x}=\begin{bmatrix}
17&51&221&238&34&119&\cdots&17
\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}
$$

[A $4\times4$ image can be represented by a vector in $\reals^{16}$]{.alert}
:::
:::

## An image is also a matrix

<svg class="diagram-image" viewBox="0 0 500 300" width="46%" role="img" aria-label="Synthetic landscape made from smooth bands"><defs><linearGradient id="image-sky" y2="1"><stop stop-color="#ecf7fc"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#78b8dc"/></linearGradient><linearGradient id="image-land" x2="1"><stop stop-color="#203d2e"/><stop offset=".5" stop-color="#75a35e"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#294a36"/></linearGradient></defs><rect x="20" y="15" width="460" height="270" rx="8" fill="url(#image-sky)"/><circle cx="365" cy="80" r="40" fill="#ffe39a"/><path d="M20 220Q120 140 230 215T480 165V285H20Z" fill="url(#image-land)"/><path d="M20 255Q120 215 240 260T480 225V285H20Z" fill="#183345" opacity=".8"/></svg>

Every grayscale pixel is one entry of a matrix:
$\mat{M}=(m_{jk})_{j=1,k=1}^{m,n}$

Images contain repeated patterns

## A matrix is an action

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 360" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Square transformed by a shear"><g stroke="#d5d5d5"><path d="M30 60H610M30 120H610M30 180H610M30 240H610M30 300H610M90 20V340M150 20V340M210 20V340M270 20V340M370 20V340M430 20V340M490 20V340M550 20V340"/></g><rect x="90" y="120" width="120" height="120" fill="#007acc" opacity=".35" stroke="#004b80" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M390 240L450 120H570L510 240Z" fill="#f39c34" opacity=".45" stroke="#a85b00" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M250 180H345" stroke="#007acc" stroke-width="7"/><polygon points="345,180 320,166 320,194" fill="#007acc"/></svg>
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
$$
\mat{A}=\begin{bmatrix}
1&\tfrac12\\
0&1
\end{bmatrix}
$$

This matrix [shears]{.alert} every vector

$$\vct{x}\longmapsto\mat{A}\vct{x}$$
:::
:::

## Predict before calculating

$$
\mat{R}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\vct{x}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}
$$

What will $\mat{R}\vct{x}$ do?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
A. reflect
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
B. rotate $90^\circ$
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
C. double in size
:::
:::

<div class="fragment key-point">$\mat{R}\vct{x}=(-1,2)^{\mathsf T}$: counterclockwise rotation by $90^\circ$</div>

## Composition is multiplication

::: {.diagram-flow}
<div class="diagram-node">object</div><div class="diagram-arrow">$\xrightarrow{\mat{A}}$</div>
<div class="diagram-node">world</div><div class="diagram-arrow">$\xrightarrow{\mat{B}}$</div>
<div class="diagram-node">camera</div><div class="diagram-arrow">$\xrightarrow{\mat{C}}$</div>
<div class="diagram-node">screen</div>
:::

Doing the transformations in sequence is one matrix action

$$
\vct{x}_{\text{screen}}
=\mat{C}\mat{B}\mat{A}\vct{x}_{\text{object}}
$$

Order matters

## Locate a source

Three sensors estimate an unknown location $(x,y)$

$$
\begin{aligned}
x+y&=6 &&\text{sensor 1}\\
2x-y&=3 &&\text{sensor 2}\\
3x&=9 &&\text{sensor 3}
\end{aligned}
$$

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 300" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Three constraint lines meeting at the point 3 comma 3"><path d="M40 260H490M40 260V20" stroke="#555" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M40 55L460 245" stroke="#007acc" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M90 260L300 20" stroke="#f39c34" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M250 20V260" stroke="#0f8b8d" stroke-width="5"/><circle cx="250" cy="150" r="10" fill="#c62828"/><text x="267" y="143" font-size="24">(3,3)</text></svg>
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
All three constraints agree

But the third is the sum of the first two

More equations do not always mean more information
:::
:::

## What does the system tell us?

::: {.question-grid}
<div><span class="diagram-label">existence</span><br>Does any solution satisfy every constraint?</div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">uniqueness</span><br>Is there exactly one solution?</div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">information</span><br>Which constraints add something new?</div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">reversibility</span><br>Can outputs determine the inputs?</div>
:::

::: {.key-point}
Solving means understanding the information in a system—not only finding numbers.
:::

## Real data miss the line

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 380" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Scatterplot with a fitted line and residuals"><path d="M55 325H585M55 325V25" stroke="#555" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M80 295L550 70" stroke="#f39c34" stroke-width="6"/><g fill="#007acc"><circle cx="110" cy="285" r="10"/><circle cx="180" cy="220" r="10"/><circle cx="255" cy="235" r="10"/><circle cx="330" cy="160" r="10"/><circle cx="405" cy="155" r="10"/><circle cx="500" cy="85" r="10"/></g><g stroke="#777" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="7 6"><path d="M180 220V247M255 235V211M330 160V175M405 155V139"/></g></svg>
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
No line passes through every point

So $\mat{A}\vct{x}=\vct{b}$ has no exact solution

What should “best” mean?
:::
:::

## Projection gives the closest answer

<svg viewBox="0 0 1000 430" width="94%" role="img" aria-label="Data vector projected perpendicularly onto a line"><defs><marker id="projection-arrowhead" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0,10 3.5,0 7" fill="#007acc"/></marker></defs><path d="M100 350L900 80" stroke="#8ba8ba" stroke-width="8"/><path d="M100 350L640 105" stroke="#007acc" stroke-width="8" marker-end="url(#projection-arrowhead)"/><path d="M100 350L525 265" stroke="#f39c34" stroke-width="8" marker-end="url(#projection-arrowhead)"/><path d="M525 265L640 105" stroke="#c62828" stroke-width="6" stroke-dasharray="10 8"/><path d="M500 270L512 300L542 288" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="4"/><text x="645" y="92" font-size="30">data vector b</text><text x="350" y="332" font-size="30">closest possible A x̂</text><text x="595" y="205" font-size="28">residual</text></svg>

$$
\min_{\vct{x}}\;\lVert\vct{b}-\mat{A}\vct{x}\rVert^2
$$

The least-squares solution is a projection; geometry identifies the smallest error

## Importance can be recursive

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 390" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Five-node directed web network"><defs><marker id="network-arrowhead" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="7" refX="8" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0,9 3.5,0 7" fill="#7895a8"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#7895a8" stroke-width="5" fill="none" marker-end="url(#network-arrowhead)"><path d="M105 100L270 170M110 285L270 210M510 90L350 170M510 300L350 220M290 170L150 110M330 170L475 100M320 225L480 285M480 285L130 285"/></g><g fill="#f8fbfd" stroke="#007acc" stroke-width="6"><circle cx="90" cy="90" r="40"/><circle cx="90" cy="300" r="40"/><circle cx="310" cy="195" r="60" fill="#d9effb"/><circle cx="530" cy="75" r="40"/><circle cx="530" cy="315" r="40"/></g><g font-size="32" text-anchor="middle"><text x="90" y="101">A</text><text x="90" y="311">B</text><text x="310" y="206">C</text><text x="530" y="86">D</text><text x="530" y="326">E</text></g></svg>
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
A page is important if important pages link to it

How can a circular definition produce a ranking?

Let the network update the scores repeatedly
:::
:::

## A steady pattern

$$
\vct{p}_{k+1}=\mat{A}\vct{p}_k
$$

::: {.diagram-flow}
<div class="diagram-node">initial scores</div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">redistribute</div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">redistribute</div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">steady scores?</div>
:::

A steady ranking satisfies

$$\mat{A}\vct{p}=\vct{p}$$

Eigenvectors identify directions that a matrix action preserves

## Where machine learning fits

::: {.diagram-flow}
<div class="diagram-node">examples<br><span class="small">vectors</span></div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">batch<br><span class="small">matrix</span></div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">$\mat{W}\vct{x}+\vct{b}$<br><span class="small">linear layer</span></div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">nonlinearity</div><div class="diagram-arrow">→</div>
<div class="diagram-node">prediction</div>
:::

Linear algebra supplies representations, transformations, geometry, and scalable operations

Machine learning also needs probability, optimization, nonlinear models, data, and judgment

# Compute responsibly

- [Almost parallel, almost unknowable](#almost-parallel-almost-unknowable)

## Almost parallel, almost unknowable

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 380" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Almost parallel constraint lines whose intersection changes dramatically"><g stroke-width="5" fill="none"><path d="M35 325L585 70" stroke="#007acc"/><path d="M35 308L585 62" stroke="#f39c34"/><path d="M35 355L585 102" stroke="#0f8b8d" stroke-dasharray="10 8"/></g><text x="340" y="48" font-size="25">tiny change in one constraint</text><path d="M380 55L460 93" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="520" cy="100" r="9" fill="#c62828"/><circle cx="120" cy="285" r="9" fill="#7b1fa2"/><text x="460" y="135" font-size="24">intersection moves far</text></svg>
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
Nearly dependent measurements contain little independent information

A tiny change in the data can cause a large change in the solution

This is [ill-conditioning]{.alert}
:::
:::

## Exact mathematics, finite arithmetic

Computers store only a finite set of numbers

$$
0.1+0.2\ne0.3
\qquad
\text{in ordinary binary floating-point arithmetic}
$$

Usually the tiny error is harmless

But a sensitive problem or unstable algorithm can amplify small errors

::: {.key-point}
A mathematically correct method can still produce an unreliable numerical answer.
:::

## Can we trust the answer?

::: {.question-grid}
<div><span class="diagram-label">model</span><br>Do the equations represent the situation?</div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">mathematics</span><br>Does a solution exist, and is it unique?</div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">problem</span><br>Is the answer sensitive to small changes?</div>
<div><span class="diagram-label">algorithm</span><br>Does the computation control error?</div>
:::
